content.value: Direction — The Honest Clone

The wave's product is a TRUSTWORTHY data plane, not merely a working pull. The finished experience: an operator runs `bp cloud workspace export --profile dev --dataset production` against guerrilla and `import --merge --with-blobs` into a fresh personal-local box, and gets a clone that (1) WORKS — content queries return, an imported asset serves HTTP 200; (2) is PROVABLY stripped — a secret-scan of both the bundle bytes and the target DB scores zero hits, and the SAME scan FIRES on a full-fidelity bundle (the positive control is the load-bearing artifact); (3) is PROVABLY convergent — a second pull is byte-identical, counts stable; (4) cannot corrupt the source — import --merge against guerrilla itself is refused server-side. Every green must be one a broken build could NOT also produce: distrust vacuous green (PDS-D20).

Priority order follows blast radius, not the dependency chain alone. dev-export is FIRST and most dangerous: it is the scrub-at-export heart — a single :copy that should be :deny is a live secret leak, so its protective test (seed webhook secret + api_token + scoped secret + ticket doc, scan RAW tar bytes for zero hits) is the wave's inner tripwire, and the :full path must stay byte-identical (md5 parity). provenance-guard is SECOND: the Bootstrap clobber is a silent data-corruption hazard that would quietly undermine 'byte-identical convergence' on the next boot — but the guard must be surgical (skip content-overwrite only on stamp-covered rows; uncovered plugin schemas still evolve normally). pull-cli is the UX front door (streamed sidecar, honest per-file report, non-zero exit on any blob failure, provenance receipt, cloud-target warning). crown-proof SEALS it live.

The scratch target IS personal-local (bin/barkpark up) — so the crown proof quietly demonstrates the twin doctrine's local home too, without pulling W3's `bp dev` verbs or G8 twin-sync into scope. That restraint is deliberate: this wave is the DATA PLANE (G1 pull + G2 blobs + G3 scrub). The verbs and offline reconcile are a later wave.
Direction debate — the rivals weighed
Three directions were developed and argued:

items.value: RIVAL A — Execute-the-spine: treat the 4 tasks as the plan, optimize for 'the pull works end to end.' Rejected as the ceiling: it under-weights the proof standard. A secret-free clone that only half-serves, or a green secret-scan that a no-op build would also pass, would read as done while being worthless. The wave's value is trust, and A does not make trust the measured thing.

RIVAL B — Twin-doctrine-forward: make offline-first Personal Local the hero, demonstrate pull-into-local with networking cut. Rejected as overreach: the bp dev verbs and G8 bp dev sync are explicitly W3 in the charter (§9, §5). This wave has no verb layer to hang an offline demo on; reaching for it now builds on absent foundations. Personal-local appears here only as the crown proof's scratch target — earned, not forced.

WINNER — The Honest Clone (a synthesis leaning security-first): the crown proof is the wave's product; the three engine slices are scaffolding judged by whether the proof can stand on them. Faithful to the charter's 'done means' (0 secrets proven by scan, prod never written, byte-identical round-trips) and to the distrust-vacuous-green doctrine. It wins because it makes the RIGHT thing — provable safety of real data — the measured outcome, without scope creep.

Where reports CONTRADICT each other or the direction

CONTRADICTION 1 (highest stakes) — what Bootstrap actually clobbers. schema-def-unique-index traces get_schema's dataset resolution through WriteScope.resolve_read_dataset_id with opts=[] to read_default_project_id, concluding Bootstrap targets the seeded Default project only. bootstrap-clobber-shape traces the same call and concludes the read is fully UNSCOPED — scope_to_workspace_global/1 is literally `do: query`, so it matches ANY workspace's row by (name, dataset) string with an arbitrary `order_by(asc_nulls_last: dataset_id) |> limit(1)` tie-break, and additionally NILs workspace_id/project_id/dataset_id because those ride as explicit nil in attrs and are all in the cast list. These cannot both be true. The first makes provenance-guard's third leg a narrow Default-slot guard; the second makes it a cross-tenant data-corruption fix that also permanently drops dataset_id on every boot. Nobody RAN it. Neither surveyor opened the wave-1 Paper's cited bootstrap-clobber-live-proof.

CONTRADICTION 2 — the dev_copy census. #4384's commit message says 18 copy tables; dev-deny-completeness counted 16 named + documents = 17; live-catalog-drift counted 16+documents=17 against a 62-table reachable set that summed exactly. An off-by-one in a commit message is harmless; an off-by-one in the actual map is a leak or a false raise.

TENSION with the direction — the ticket-deny positive control. The charter and the wave lean on `deny_types: [ticket]` as a demonstrated filter. Guerrilla has exactly ONE ticket document and it is a DRAFT. I ran GET /v1/data/counts/production against guerrilla during this digest: the response carries NO ticket key at all (counts are published-perspective only, returning command/document/metric/paper/tag/task = 6 types / 2555 docs, against the raw DB census of 11 types / 2769). So a build that omitted the ticket WHERE clause entirely would produce an IDENTICAL published count diff. The ticket leg of the crown proof is vacuous against live data unless the harness seeds a PUBLISHED ticket first or scans raw bytes for the known ticket doc_id.

TENSION with the direction — 'byte-identical convergence'. merge-import-convergence establishes that E3/allowlist stay bare ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in BOTH modes by deliberate design (first-workspace-wins on shared string-keyed rows). DO NOTHING resurrects a deleted row but never corrects a drifted one, and the crown proof injects no drift between its two pulls — so the convergence criterion passes whether or not E3 reconciles. The wave must either scope the claim honestly (root+E1+E2 converge on CONTENT; E3 converges on PRESENCE only) or prove the boundary with a control.

content.value: Direction — The Honest Clone

The wave's product is a TRUSTWORTHY data plane, not merely a working pull. The finished experience: an operator runs `bp cloud workspace export --profile dev --dataset production` against guerrilla and `import --merge --with-blobs` into a fresh personal-local box, and gets a clone that (1) WORKS — content queries return, an imported asset serves HTTP 200; (2) is PROVABLY stripped — a secret-scan of both the bundle bytes and the target DB scores zero hits, and the SAME scan FIRES on a full-fidelity bundle (the positive control is the load-bearing artifact); (3) is PROVABLY convergent — a second pull is byte-identical, counts stable; (4) cannot corrupt the source — import --merge against guerrilla itself is refused server-side. Every green must be one a broken build could NOT also produce: distrust vacuous green (PDS-D20).

Priority order follows blast radius, not the dependency chain alone. dev-export is FIRST and most dangerous: it is the scrub-at-export heart — a single :copy that should be :deny is a live secret leak, so its protective test (seed webhook secret + api_token + scoped secret + ticket doc, scan RAW tar bytes for zero hits) is the wave's inner tripwire, and the :full path must stay byte-identical (md5 parity). provenance-guard is SECOND: the Bootstrap clobber is a silent data-corruption hazard that would quietly undermine 'byte-identical convergence' on the next boot — but the guard must be surgical (skip content-overwrite only on stamp-covered rows; uncovered plugin schemas still evolve normally). pull-cli is the UX front door (streamed sidecar, honest per-file report, non-zero exit on any blob failure, provenance receipt, cloud-target warning). crown-proof SEALS it live.

The scratch target IS personal-local (bin/barkpark up) — so the crown proof quietly demonstrates the twin doctrine's local home too, without pulling W3's `bp dev` verbs or G8 twin-sync into scope. That restraint is deliberate: this wave is the DATA PLANE (G1 pull + G2 blobs + G3 scrub). The verbs and offline reconcile are a later wave.

PDS-D31 — Deny is a COPY-time SKIP, exports are strictly serialized, and only ONE full bundle is ever taken. Why: 1.83 GB peak on a 3.8 GB box means a post-filter or a concurrent export takes down the live API.

PDS-D37 — Task 24913529 (WorkspaceBundle streaming) is sequenced OUT of this wave. Why: it rewrites the exact functions dev-export and provenance-guard touch.

A teardown on a root whose scratch.env was missing or truncated therefore killed whatever held port 4000 — the host's shared dev server, the one thing the script's header promises never to touch — and then printed 'teardown: PASS'. It did exactly that to this host's dev server during review. PDS Epic — Wave 2: The Honest Clone (2026-07-19)

WAVE STATUS: ROUND 1 COMPLETE — reviewed, graded A-, ready for the lead to merge. Three slices built and adversarially reviewed (pds-w1-dev-export, pds-w2-scratch-harness, pds-w2-secret-scan); rounds 2 and 3 (provenance-guard, pull-cli, crown-proof) are deferrals the lead dispatches as their deps land on main. The wish

Land the PDS data plane's pull loop end to end and PROVE it against real data. The dev-profile partition, merge-import, path-preserving blob write, and the personal-local boot are already on main. Wave 2 makes the engine actually consume them: a profile-aware, dataset-scoped export that scrubs at the source; provenance stamped onto pulled datasets plus a guard against the boot-time Bootstrap schema clobber; a bp cloud workspace pull dialect (profile/dataset/merge/with-blobs) with a streamed blob sidecar; and the crown proof — a live guerrilla dataset pulled into a scratch personal-local box, assets serving, zero secrets, byte-identical on re-pull.

Grounding — what main actually says (read, not assumed)

• Dev-profile partition is LIVE on main (workspace_bundle/catalog.ex): @dev_copy / @dev_deny / @dev_scrub (empty) + documents {:copy, deny_types: [ticket]}. Fail-closed: dev_action/1 returns :deny for any unclassified table, and assert_dev_partition!/2 RAISES on any gap, phantom, or unreviewed composite PK. search_intel_events is :deny; secrets/api_tokens/webhooks/access_grants/audit/revisions/mutation_events all :deny. CLASSIFICATION DATA ONLY — the exporter does not read it yet.
• export/2 IGNORES its opts today: do_export(%Workspace{} = ws, _opts) — no profile, no dataset. The dev-export slice hooks profile/dataset into do_export → copy_out_sql / copy_where and the controller export action (which also passes no query params yet).
• Merge import LANDED (#4385): import_bundle/2 with mode :clean|:merge; merge_upsert via ON CONFLICT (order_columns) DO UPDATE for copy tables; E3/allowlist stay DO NOTHING both modes. Controller merge path is FAIL-CLOSED opt-in: 403 bundle_import_disabled unless :allow_bundle_import. Registered codes: bundle_import_disabled / invalid_mode / workspace_slug_conflict.
• Blob path-preserving write + personal-local fresh boot LANDED (#4383): KEK autogen, missing-blob 404, runtime media dir, path-verbatim blob PUT that refuses empty body, allow_bundle_import plumbed.
• HAZARD confirmed by read: Barkpark.Plugins.Bootstrap.register_all_schemas/0 upserts every plugin schema each boot via Content.upsert_schema keyed on (name, dataset) — Repo.update for existing rows. Whether it clobbers a PULLED workspace's customized schema cross-tenant depends on whether the schema_definitions unique index is (name, dataset) GLOBAL or workspace-scoped — a survey question, load-bearing for whether provenance-guard's bootstrap-guard is real.
• GET /v1/counts (axi-b2 #4377) landed — candidate source for the crown proof's per-type count diff.

Direction — The Honest Clone

The wave's product is a TRUSTWORTHY data plane, not merely a working pull. The finished experience: an operator runs `bp cloud workspace export --profile dev --dataset production` against guerrilla and `import --merge --with-blobs` into a fresh personal-local box, and gets a clone that (1) WORKS — content queries return, an imported asset serves HTTP 200; (2) is PROVABLY stripped — a secret-scan of both the bundle bytes and the target DB scores zero hits, and the SAME scan FIRES on a full-fidelity bundle (the positive control is the load-bearing artifact); (3) is PROVABLY convergent — a second pull is byte-identical, counts stable; (4) cannot corrupt the source — import --merge against guerrilla itself is refused server-side. Every green must be one a broken build could NOT also produce: distrust vacuous green (PDS-D20).

Priority order follows blast radius, not the dependency chain alone. dev-export is FIRST and most dangerous: it is the scrub-at-export heart — a single :copy that should be :deny is a live secret leak, so its protective test (seed webhook secret + api_token + scoped secret + ticket doc, scan RAW tar bytes for zero hits) is the wave's inner tripwire, and the :full path must stay byte-identical (md5 parity). provenance-guard is SECOND: the Bootstrap clobber is a silent data-corruption hazard that would quietly undermine 'byte-identical convergence' on the next boot — but the guard must be surgical (skip content-overwrite only on stamp-covered rows; uncovered plugin schemas still evolve normally). pull-cli is the UX front door (streamed sidecar, honest per-file report, non-zero exit on any blob failure, provenance receipt, cloud-target warning). crown-proof SEALS it live.

The scratch target IS personal-local (bin/barkpark up) — so the crown proof quietly demonstrates the twin doctrine's local home too, without pulling W3's `bp dev` verbs or G8 twin-sync into scope. Direction — The Honest Clone

The wave's product is a TRUSTWORTHY data plane, not merely a working pull. The finished experience: an operator runs `bp cloud workspace export --profile dev --dataset production` against guerrilla and `import --merge --with-blobs` into a fresh personal-local box, and gets a clone that (1) WORKS — content queries return, an imported asset serves HTTP 200; (2) is PROVABLY stripped — a secret-scan of both the bundle bytes and the target DB scores zero hits, and the SAME scan FIRES on a full-fidelity bundle (the positive control is the load-bearing artifact); (3) is PROVABLY convergent — a second pull is byte-identical, counts stable; (4) cannot corrupt the source — import --merge against guerrilla itself is refused server-side. Every green must be one a broken build could NOT also produce: distrust vacuous green (PDS-D20).

Priority order follows blast radius, not the dependency chain alone. dev-export is FIRST and most dangerous: it is the scrub-at-export heart — a single :copy that should be :deny is a live secret leak, so its protective test (seed webhook secret + api_token + scoped secret + ticket doc, scan RAW tar bytes for zero hits) is the wave's inner tripwire, and the :full path must stay byte-identical (md5 parity). provenance-guard is SECOND: the Bootstrap clobber is a silent data-corruption hazard that would quietly undermine 'byte-identical convergence' on the next boot — but the guard must be surgical (skip content-overwrite only on stamp-covered rows; uncovered plugin schemas still evolve normally). pull-cli is the UX front door (streamed sidecar, honest per-file report, non-zero exit on any blob failure, provenance receipt, cloud-target warning). crown-proof SEALS it live.

The scratch target IS personal-local (bin/barkpark up) — so the crown proof quietly demonstrates the twin doctrine's local home too, without pulling W3's `bp dev` verbs or G8 twin-sync into scope. That restraint is deliberate: this wave is the DATA PLANE (G1 pull + G2 blobs + G3 scrub). The verbs and offline reconcile are a later wave.

Direction debate — the rivals weighed

Three directions were developed and argued:

  • RIVAL A — Execute-the-spine: treat the 4 tasks as the plan, optimize for 'the pull works end to end.' Rejected as the ceiling: it under-weights the proof standard. A secret-free clone that only half-serves, or a green secret-scan that a no-op build would also pass, would read as done while being worthless. The wave's value is trust, and A does not make trust the measured thing.
  • RIVAL B — Twin-doctrine-forward: make offline-first Personal Local the hero, demonstrate pull-into-local with networking cut. Rejected as overreach: the bp dev verbs and G8 bp dev sync are explicitly W3 in the charter (§9, §5). This wave has no verb layer to hang an offline demo on; reaching for it now builds on absent foundations. Personal-local appears here only as the crown proof's scratch target — earned, not forced.
  • WINNER — The Honest Clone (a synthesis leaning security-first): the crown proof is the wave's product; the three engine slices are scaffolding judged by whether the proof can stand on them. Faithful to the charter's 'done means' (0 secrets proven by scan, prod never written, byte-identical round-trips) and to the distrust-vacuous-green doctrine. It wins because it makes the RIGHT thing — provable safety of real data — the measured outcome, without scope creep.

Sharpest attack on the winner: the crown proof depends on a chain of live facts that could each abort it before it demonstrates anything — a NEW guerrilla tenant table since the 2026-07-19 census would RAISE the export sentinel; guerrilla's default/production may not carry enough content or plaintext-secret webhooks to make the positive control fire; allow_bundle_import may be mis-set on either box; and the Bootstrap clobber may not actually fire (if the schema unique index is workspace-scoped), making provenance-guard's third leg dead weight. The wave absorbs this by front-loading ALL of these into the survey as live-census questions — the fleets settle them BEFORE builders fly, and Decide rescopes provenance-guard if the clobber proves inert. The direction does not hedge; it aims the survey at exactly what could kill it.

DEBRIEF — Review phase, 2026-07-19

One Fable reviewed all three green slices in its own worktree, branched each as <branch>-r, chased the builders' own stated doubts first, fixed what it found in place, and re-ran every gate on its final state. Grade: A-.

What shipped, per slice

  • pds-w1-dev-export → loop-epic/profile-aware-dataset-granular-export-de-0-r (review commit f1b552115). The engine slice, and the strongest of the three. Profile (:full default | :dev) and dataset (slug) now reach four hook points, and the controller finally passes its query params (before this the action matched only workspace_slug and do_export/2 discarded opts outright — zero caller intent reached the engine). PDS-D31 is a real pre-loop SKIP proven by telemetry capture of every SQL statement (exactly 17 COPYs; the denied tables appear in NO query, with the full profile as the foil). PDS-D28's dev_action/1 flattening trap is pinned by a unit test. PDS-D27's cascade is live-derived from pg_constraint. PDS-D29's arbiter refuses ambiguity with a named ExportScopeError carrying machine-branchable codes, and reproduces the live guerrilla dataset_slugs_for trap as a test. REVIEW FIX: Catalog.document_fk_columns/2 matched any FK whose referenced TABLE is documents without checking WHICH column — but the predicate the caller emits is dtd.id = t.<col>, so an FK to some other documents key, or one leg of a composite FK, would have been returned and compared against the wrong column. conkey is now paired to confkey by ordinality with the referenced attribute pinned to id. Gate re-run green: 50/50 on the three gate files, 87/87 with the controller suite. INDEPENDENT NON-VACUITY CHECK: neutering narrow_slugs to the identity turns exactly the two dataset-narrowing tests RED and nothing else — the assertions are load-bearing.
  • pds-w2-scratch-harness → loop-epic/a-scratch-personal-local-target-boots-an-1-r (review commits 254776d9a, 9e4dc0007). All five run-proven traps encoded with actionable failures, and the media-isolation negative control is genuine — it prints upload_dir() with and without BARKPARK_MEDIA_DIR and asserts the un-isolated half resolves to the RUNNING TREE, so the isolated green cannot be free. REVIEW FOUND A LIVE HAZARD, by running teardown rather than reading it: bin/barkpark stop → stop_server falls back to listener_pid when its pidfile is stale, and listener_pid reads $PORT, which DEFAULTS TO 4000. A teardown on a root whose scratch.env was missing or truncated therefore killed whatever held port 4000 — the host's shared dev server, the one thing the script's header promises never to touch — and then printed 'teardown: PASS'. It did exactly that to this host's dev server during review. Teardown now refuses unless it knows this root's own two ports (run-proven: exit 1, tree preserved, 4000 untouched); a failed port/orphan assert no longer removes the tree (yanking a data dir out from under a live process destroys the evidence for the leak the assert just found); and the orphan check is fixed-string ps|grep -F instead of a regex over a caller-supplied path. The same hazard still lives in bin/barkpark for every other caller — filed as pds-barkpark-stop-4000-fallback.
  • pds-w2-secret-scan → loop-epic/a-value-based-secret-scan-with-a-control-2-r (review commit bf75ec00b). Value-based, never column-name-based; the positive control is seeded locally so no live guerrilla export is spent, and it is measured on three exit paths, including a --simulate-broken-instrument tripwire that proves the control CAN fail. The PDS-D25 honesty holds: the dev summary says 'mechanism = table DENY … nothing here was scrubbed', and both limits print on every run. REVIEW FIX: a value-taking flag with nothing after it fell through ${2:-} and died on shift 2 — under set -e that is exit 1 with ZERO output, and 1 is the HIT code, so 'scan --bundle b --value' read as 'secrets found' while nothing had been scanned. New guard exits 2 and names the flag. Also: control now requires openssl up front (it generates the run's fresh ammo; without it the seed would silently be an EMPTY secret and the control would 'pass' against nothing), plus one shellcheck quoting fix. All three exit paths independently re-run green on the fixed bytes: control 0 (fires on tables/webhooks.copy AND the target DB, clean on the deny-shaped bundle), broken-instrument 3, missing-value 2.

Cross-slice coherence

The three slices cohere: disjoint file sets, shared PDS-D decision vocabulary, shared anti-vacuity doctrine (every deny paired with a positive control; every instrument proven able to fail). One real gap was found and closed: pds-secret-scan.sh takes --db <conninfo> and the crown proof's step 4 must score the TARGET DB, but scratch.env named only the HTTP base, token and media dir — every consumer would have re-derived barkpark-pg's PG_HOST/PG_DB/PG_USER defaults by hand. scratch.env now exports PDS_SCRATCH_DB, mirroring the BARKPARK_PG_DB/_USER overrides rather than hardcoding them.

What did NOT happen, and why

  • Nothing stalled. Three round-1 slices were dispatched and three came back green.
  • Rounds 2 and 3 were not built BY DESIGN (the sequenced-rounds law): pds-w1-provenance-guard and pds-w1-pull-cli both depend on pds-w1-dev-export being ON MAIN, and pds-w1-crown-proof depends on all four. Their tasks are open with correct content.dependencies, so bp task ready strands them until their deps merge.
  • THE HONEST SHORTFALL: this wave's own standard is 'the crown proof is non-negotiable — the wave is not done without live run output.' No live guerrilla-into-scratch pull ran. What round 1 delivered is the export dialect the proof consumes plus BOTH instruments the proof needs, each with a control that fires. That is the right round-1 outcome under the sequencing law, but it means the wave's headline claim is still unpaid. The next wave owns it, and until it runs, nothing in this Paper should be read as evidence that a real pull is secret-free.
  • Known real-data risks carried into the crown proof, both flagged by the dev-export builder and filed as task-1e76a21eb8a17d43: (1) documents.dataset_id is NULLABLE, and PDS-D7 binds Group-A to the canonical column, so a legacy NULL-dataset_id row silently does not travel in a dataset-scoped pull — a guerrilla census is needed BEFORE the crown proof; (2) Group-C travels workspace-whole under --dataset per the binding PDS-D7 ruling, so a dataset-scoped bundle carries edges referencing documents that were never exported. Neither aborts an import (replica role, FK triggers off) but both leave dangling rows. The builder had the machinery to narrow Group-C and deliberately did not deviate from the ruling; the current behavior is asserted explicitly in a test so a later change is a visible diff.
  • The {:scrub_fields, fields} select-list NULL path is implemented but DATA-UNTESTED — @dev_scrub is empty in W1 and the partition is not injectable into the exporter. Four mechanically obvious lines, but untested code.

Ledger audit

  • All three slice tasks: claimed before work, criteria stamped AS THEY WERE PROVEN (not batched), lifecycle left in_progress with the 'PR merged' criterion open for the LEAD. Evidence text is specific and checkable — it names files, test titles, exit codes and counts, not adjectives. No ledger lies found; no ledger fixes were needed.
  • The four deferred round-≥2 tasks are open with correct content.dependencies (the wave-1 review's fix held), so none is prematurely claimable.
  • Builders filed their own follow-ups honestly: task-1e76a21eb8a17d43 (Group-C orphans + NULL dataset_id census) and pds-w2-scratch-harness-ci (the scheduled round-trip job the charter already names).
  • No task outside this wave was touched. Review filed one new published child: pds-barkpark-stop-4000-fallback (priority 2) — the bin/barkpark stop port-4000 fallback that review reproduced live.

Grade — A-

What earns it: the anti-vacuity doctrine was actually practised rather than cited. The D31 skip is proven by capturing every SQL statement the export issues, not by inspecting the manifest. Every deny is paired with a full-profile positive control asserting the row IS present. The secret scan ships a tripwire proving the control can fail. The scratch harness's negative control shows the un-isolated blast target FIRING. The dataset arbiter reproduces the live guerrilla trap as a test rather than trusting the brief's account of it. Builders' self-reviews were unusually honest, and every doubt they raised turned out to be worth chasing. The engine slice's full-fidelity path is held byte-identical by an explicit omitted-vs-:full dump-for-dump equality assertion on top of the md5 tripwire.

What holds it back from an A: two of three slices shipped a defect that only running them exposed — the harness silently killed the host's dev server and reported PASS, and the scan returned the HIT exit code with no output on a mistyped flag. Both are exactly the class of failure these tools exist to rule out (an answer a broken run could also produce), and both were found by exercising rather than reading, which is what the wave's own doctrine demanded of the builders. Beyond that: the crown proof — the wave's stated product — has not run, so the headline trust claim is still unpaid; the scrub_fields path is untested code; and the secret scan's fixture bundle is hand-built in the bp-export-v1 shape rather than produced by Archive.pack, so container-layout drift would go unnoticed until the crown proof scans a real bundle. No bloat: three slices, three files' worth of real surface, no speculative scaffolding.

What the next wave takes — dispatch order

  • MERGE ROUND 1 FIRST, in any order (disjoint files): the three -r branches. The lead closes the 'PR merged' criterion on each of pds-w1-dev-export, pds-w2-scratch-harness, pds-w2-secret-scan. Note that guerrilla auto-deploys on api/** merge, so the export dialect goes live with the dev-export merge.
  • THEN, as their deps land: pds-w1-provenance-guard and pds-w1-pull-cli both unblock on the dev-export merge and have disjoint file sets (api/lib/barkpark/tenancy + plugins vs internal/cli), so they dispatch in PARALLEL. Coordinate internal/cli via task claims — the Studio and GUI-remake cycles are concurrent.
  • THEN pds-w1-crown-proof, once all four of its deps are on main. Before it runs: re-verify export against the freshly deployed guerrilla, re-run assert_partition!/assert_dev_partition! at the branch point, assert schema_migrations parity between guerrilla and the scratch target BEFORE the first COPY, and do the NULL-dataset_id census that task-1e76a21eb8a17d43 asks for. Consume the two instruments; do not rebuild them. scratch.env now hands the proof PDS_SCRATCH_DB for step 4's target-DB scan.
  • Worth folding into the crown-proof run or the wave after: pds-barkpark-stop-4000-fallback (the bin/barkpark hazard, unfixed outside the PDS harness) and pds-w2-scratch-harness-ci (nothing in CI protects the harness against a rename in bin/barkpark, runtime.exs's media block, or the api_tokens shape).
